standards.standard_name: The organization respects the rights of the individual served

findings.description: The organization informs the individual served of the individual's rights
findings.finding: No documentation found throughout the entire clinical record indicating that patient rights were communicated to the patient. Searched biopsychosocial assessment, all progress notes, and admission documentation - no evidence of rights information being provided.
findings.remediation: Document that patient rights were provided and explained to patient, including receipt of written rights information

findings.description: If an individual served is disoriented or lacks capacity to understand rights at the time of entry, they are informed again when they are able to understand
findings.finding: Patient presented with cognitive impairment and confusion at admission (BAC 0.31, CIWA-Ar 18, intermittent confusion regarding timeline) but no documentation shows rights were re-communicated once orientation and cognition improved.
findings.remediation: Develop process to re-inform patients of rights when capacity is restored; document when rights were re-communicated after cognitive clearing

findings.description: The organization respects the cultural and personal values, beliefs, and preferences of the individual served
findings.finding: Assessment includes some cultural information but is incomplete. Spiritual/cultural assessment documents loss of faith and Catholic upbringing but fails to explore cultural preferences related to treatment approach or other cultural values that should inform care planning.

citations.text: Patient reports loss of faith — "I stopped believing in anything a long time ago." Beliefs/practices to incorporate into therapy: None identified at this time. Patient was raised Catholic but has no current practice.
citations.relevance: Shows some spiritual assessment but lacks comprehensive cultural values exploration

findings.remediation: Complete comprehensive cultural assessment including treatment preferences, cultural practices, dietary needs, and other values that should inform treatment planning

standards.standard_name: The organization respects the right of the individual served to receive information in a manner the individual understands

findings.description: The organization provides information to the individual served in a manner tailored to the individual's language and ability to understand
findings.finding: No documentation indicates that information was provided in a manner tailored to patient's understanding level or that staff assessed comprehension. Patient has cognitive impairments noted but no accommodation strategies documented.
findings.remediation: Document assessment of patient's comprehension level and communication adaptations made; ensure information is provided at appropriate literacy level

findings.description: The organization provides interpreting and translation services, as necessary
findings.finding: Patient's primary language is English and no interpreting services were needed based on documented language preference.

citations.text: Language: English
citations.relevance: Documents patient's primary language as English, indicating no translation services needed

findings.description: The organization communicates with the individual served who has vision, speech, hearing, or cognitive impairments in a manner that meets the needs of that individual
findings.finding: Patient has documented cognitive impairments (intermittent confusion, poor concentration, impaired judgment) but no documentation shows communication was adapted to accommodate these cognitive limitations.
findings.remediation: Document communication adaptations made for patients with cognitive impairments; ensure information delivery accounts for concentration and comprehension limitations

standards.standard_name: The organization respects the right of the individual served to collaborate in decisions about their care, treatment, or services

findings.description: The organization involves the individual served in making decisions about their care, treatment, or services
findings.finding: Some evidence of patient involvement in treatment decisions exists, particularly regarding discharge planning and medication discussions, but formal shared decision-making process is not consistently documented across treatment planning.

citations.text: Patient tearful but affect notably brighter than previous sessions. Reports she spoke with brother by phone and he reiterated his offer for her to come to Denver: "He said he'd help me find a job and go to meetings with me."
citations.relevance: Shows patient involvement in discharge planning decisions

citations.text: Denver discharge plan with brother represents the most viable pathway to sustained recovery — sober environment, family support, geographic distance from boyfriend and using network.
citations.relevance: Indicates patient input was considered in discharge planning but doesn't document the collaborative decision-making process

findings.remediation: Document systematic involvement of patient in all treatment decisions; establish formal shared decision-making process for treatment planning

findings.description: The organization respects the right of the individual served or surrogate decision-maker to refuse care, treatment, or services in accordance with law and regulation
findings.finding: No documentation found regarding patient's right to refuse treatment or how refusals would be handled. No evidence that this right was communicated to the patient.
findings.remediation: Document patient education regarding right to refuse treatment; establish clear process for handling treatment refusals in accordance with regulations

standards.standard_name: The organization honors the right of the individual served to give or withhold informed consent

findings.description: The informed consent process includes a discussion about the proposed care, treatment, or services; goals and potential benefits and risks; reasonable alternatives and risks/benefits of alternatives and not receiving care
findings.finding: No documentation of informed consent process found. No evidence that proposed treatments, goals, benefits, risks, or alternatives were discussed with patient in a formal informed consent process.
findings.remediation: Implement and document comprehensive informed consent process covering all required elements: proposed treatments, goals, benefits, risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusing treatment

standards.standard_name: The organization respects the right of the individual served to receive information about the staff responsible for the individual's care, treatment, or services

findings.description: The organization informs the individual served of the name of the staff member who has primary responsibility for the individual's care and the name of staff members who will provide care
findings.finding: While clinician names appear in documentation (andrew c), there is no evidence that the patient was formally informed about who has primary responsibility for care or which staff members would be providing services.
findings.remediation: Document that patient was informed of primary clinician and treatment team members; establish process to communicate staff roles and responsibilities to patients

standards.standard_name: The organization maintains complete and accurate clinical/case records.

findings.description: The clinical/case record includes information needed to support the diagnosis or condition; justify care, treatment, or services; document the course and result of care; and promote continuity among staff and providers.

However, the record lacks documented results or outcomes of specific treatments provided, and mental status exam is explicitly noted as 'Not documented' which is required for complete diagnostic support.

standards.standard_name: The individual served receives education and training specific to the individual's needs and abilities consistent with the care, treatment, or services provided.

findings.description: Education provided is based on the needs and abilities of the individual served.
findings.finding: No documentation of formal patient education being provided. While treatment activities are documented, there is no evidence of structured educational content tailored to the patient's specific needs and abilities.
findings.remediation: Implement and document formal patient education sessions addressing the patient's specific substance use disorders, trauma history, and medical conditions with content tailored to her abilities

findings.description: The assessment of learning needs addresses the individual's cultural and religious beliefs, emotional barriers, desire and motivation to learn, physical or cognitive limitations, and barriers to communication.

findings.remediation: Conduct and document formal learning needs assessment addressing cultural/religious beliefs, emotional barriers, motivation to learn, cognitive limitations, and communication barriers

findings.description: Based on the assessed needs and abilities of the individual served and the organization's scope of care, treatment, or services, the individual is educated about the following: The plan for care, treatment, or services; Basic health practices and safety; The safe and effective use of medications; Nutrition interventions, modified diets, and oral health, as needed; Habilitation or rehabilitation techniques to help them reach the maximum level of independence possible.
findings.finding: No documentation of formal education provided on required topics. While medications are prescribed and nutritional concerns noted, there is no evidence of structured patient education on treatment plan, health practices, medication safety, nutrition, or rehabilitation techniques.
findings.remediation: Provide and document comprehensive patient education covering treatment plan, health practices and safety, medication management, nutritional needs, and recovery techniques

standards.standard_name: The organization screens all individuals served for their nutritional status.

findings.description: The organization screens all individuals served to identify those for whom a nutritional assessment is indicated. standards.standard_name: The organization has a plan for care, treatment, or services that reflects the assessed needs, strengths, preferences, and goals of the individual served.

findings.finding: No formal treatment plan document exists. While comprehensive assessment information is available and various treatment activities are documented in progress notes, there is no structured treatment plan that organizes this information into a coherent plan reflecting assessed needs, strengths, preferences, and goals.
findings.remediation: Develop a formal written treatment plan that incorporates assessment findings into a structured plan addressing patient's needs, strengths, preferences, and goals.

findings.description: The plan for care, treatment, or services includes the following: Goals that are expressed in a manner that captures the individual's words or ideas; Goals that build on the individual's strengths; Factors that support the transition to community integration when identified as a need during assessment; The criteria and process for the individual's expected successful transfer and/or discharge/termination of services, which the organization discusses with the individual.

findings.remediation: Create treatment plan with goals expressed in patient's words, goals that build on identified strengths, community integration planning, and specific discharge criteria discussed with the patient.

findings.description: The objectives of the plan for care, treatment, or services meet the following criteria: They are based on identified goals; They include identified steps to achieve the goal(s); They are sufficiently specific to assess the progress of the individual served; They are expressed in terms that provide indices of progress.
findings.finding: No formal treatment objectives exist. Without a treatment plan containing formal goals, there are no objectives that meet the specified criteria for goal-based, specific, measurable objectives with progress indices.
findings.remediation: Develop specific, measurable objectives for each treatment goal that include action steps and progress indicators.

findings.description: The organization reevaluates and, when necessary, revises the goals and objectives of the plan for care, treatment, or services based on change(s) in the individual's needs, preferences, and goals and the individual's response to care, treatment, or services. findings.finding: No treatment plan exists to reevaluate or revise. While progress notes document ongoing assessment and plan modifications, there is no formal treatment plan with goals and objectives that can be systematically reevaluated.
findings.remediation: Establish treatment plan with goals and objectives, then implement systematic reevaluation process at specified intervals per organizational policy.

findings.description: Reasons for deferring a goal, or the objectives leading toward or related to a goal, are documented.
findings.finding: No treatment plan with formal goals exists, therefore there are no documented deferrals or reasons for deferring goals or objectives.
findings.remediation: Once treatment plan is established, document any deferrals of goals or objectives with rationale.

findings.description: The organization provides care, treatment, or services for each individual served according to the plan for care, treatment, or services.

findings.remediation: Develop treatment plan and ensure all care, treatment, and services are delivered according to the plan and documented as such.

findings.description: As relevant to care, treatment, or services, the assessment data collected about the individual's emotional and behavioral functioning include at least the following: History of emotional functioning; History of behavioral functioning; Addictive behaviors as a primary or a co-occurring condition(s), including the use of alcohol, other drugs, gambling, or other addictive behaviors by the individual served and family members; Current emotional functioning; Current behavioral functioning
findings.finding: The assessment comprehensively covers all required elements of emotional and behavioral functioning history and current status, plus detailed addictive behaviors assessment for both patient and family.

citations.text: Affective: Persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, tearfulness, severe anxiety, constricted affect. PHQ-9: 18 (moderately severe). GAD-7: 15 (severe).
citations.relevance: Documents current emotional functioning with standardized assessments

citations.text: Summary of use: Alcohol: onset age 15, current daily use 750mL-1L vodka for past 2 years, morning drinking to prevent withdrawal. Opioids: onset age 22 with prescribed Percocet, transitioned to heroin age 24, IV fentanyl age 28, current use 1-2g IV fentanyl daily. Benzodiazepines: onset age 25, initially prescribed, escalated to 4-6mg alprazolam daily
citations.relevance: Documents detailed addictive behaviors history

citations.text: Mother: Alcohol use disorder and depression. Father: Deceased at age 49 from liver failure secondary to alcoholism. Brother: In recovery from opioid use disorder, 3 years sober. Extensive family history of substance use disorders across both parental lines.
citations.relevance: Documents family addictive behaviors history

findings.description: The assessment data collected include the individual's short- and long-term personal goal(s)
findings.finding: Long-term goals are documented but short-term personal goals are not clearly identified or documented in the assessment.

citations.text: Changes desired: Patient has expressed interest in peer support and recovery community. Stated she wants to 'help people like me someday' and asked about peer support specialist training.
citations.relevance: Documents long-term career/helping goals

findings.remediation: Document specific short-term recovery goals such as housing stability, family reconnection, or immediate treatment objectives in patient's own words

findings.description: When indicated, the following evaluations are conducted: Mental status; Psychological; Psychiatric; Intellectual and cognitive functioning
findings.finding: Mental status exam is referenced in progress notes but not formally documented in the biopsychosocial assessment. Psychiatric evaluation appears to have occurred based on medication management but formal psychological or cognitive evaluations are not documented.

citations.text: Mental Status Exam: Not documented
citations.relevance: Explicitly states mental status exam was not documented

citations.text: Patient presents as thin, underweight female appearing older than stated age of 37. Dressed in hospital gown, hygiene fair. Oriented x3, intermittently confused regarding timeline of recent events.
citations.relevance: Shows mental status elements are assessed but not formally documented

findings.remediation: Complete formal mental status examination documentation and consider psychological evaluation given trauma history and cognitive symptoms

findings.description: Family members are invited to participate in the assessment process as relevant to the care, treatment, or services provided, and the age and preference of the individual served
findings.finding: There is no documentation that family members were invited to participate in the assessment process, despite having a supportive brother who could provide relevant information.
findings.remediation: Document whether family participation was offered and patient's response, particularly given brother's supportive role and willingness to help with recovery planning

standards.standard_name: The organization identifies individuals who may have experienced trauma, abuse, neglect, or exploitation

findings.description: The organization identifies individuals who may have experienced trauma, abuse, neglect, or exploitation during initial screening and assessment and on an ongoing basis
findings.finding: Patient's trauma history is clearly identified during initial assessment with documentation of childhood abuse, intimate partner violence, and trauma-related symptoms driving substance use.

citations.text: Reports severe anxiety, persistent nightmares about childhood abuse occurring nightly, and chronic low mood.
citations.relevance: Identifies childhood abuse trauma

citations.text: Current boyfriend is an active substance user and perpetrator of intimate partner violence. Patient reports he 'doesn't hit me that much anymore but he controls everything.'
citations.relevance: Identifies current intimate partner violence

citations.text: Patient reports substance use as self-medication for trauma-related symptoms: 'I started using to not feel.'
citations.relevance: Links trauma to substance use as presenting problem

findings.description: The organization assesses the individual who may have experienced trauma, abuse, neglect, or exploitation or refers the individual for such assessment
findings.finding: Patient is being assessed for trauma through multiple clinical interventions including Seeking Safety group participation, safety planning with DV advocate, and planned EMDR readiness assessment.

citations.text: Continue Seeking Safety group
citations.relevance: Documents trauma-informed group therapy participation

citations.text: Completed initial safety plan with DV advocate.
citations.relevance: Documents specialized IPV assessment and safety planning

citations.text: Begin EMDR readiness assessment once withdrawal fully resolved
citations.relevance: Documents plan for specialized trauma therapy assessment

standards.standard_name: Reassessment

findings.description: The organization reassesses each individual served, as needed
findings.finding: Patient is being reassessed regularly through progress notes documenting changes in clinical status, standardized assessments (PHQ-9, GAD-7), and planned treatment plan updates.

citations.text: PHQ-9: 16 (moderately severe, improved from 18 at admission). GAD-7: 14 (severe).
citations.relevance: Documents reassessment using standardized tools with comparison to baseline

citations.text: PHQ-9: 14 (moderate, down from 18 at admission). GAD-7: 12 (moderate, down from 15).
citations.relevance: Shows ongoing reassessment tracking clinical improvement

citations.text: Update treatment plan at scheduled review (04/10) — add IPV/safety as formal treatment plan problem
citations.relevance: Documents planned formal reassessment and treatment plan updates

standards.standard_name: The organization has a process to provide medical histories, physical examinations, and diagnostic and laboratory tests

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The program collects toxicological specimens in a manner that demonstrates trust and respect while taking reasonable steps to prevent falsification of samples
findings.finding: Toxicological testing was performed (admission UDS documented) but there is no documentation of the collection process, procedures to prevent falsification, or how trust and respect were demonstrated during collection.

citations.text: Admission UDS positive for fentanyl, oxycodone, benzodiazepines (alprazolam metabolites), and THC.
citations.relevance: Documents that toxicological testing occurred

findings.remediation: Document the UDS collection process, including measures taken to prevent falsification and how patient dignity was maintained during collection

findings.description: For programs providing medications for substance use disorders: When initiating medications for substance use disorders, the program makes certain that medical assessments and testing are done according to current national guidelines established for the treatment being used
findings.finding: Patient is receiving buprenorphine 16mg but there is no documentation of pre-initiation medical assessments or testing according to national guidelines (such as baseline QTc, liver function assessment for buprenorphine candidacy, or COWS scoring before induction).
findings.remediation: Document medical assessments performed before buprenorphine initiation including baseline EKG, comprehensive metabolic panel, and COWS assessment per SAMHSA guidelines

standards.standard_name: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The assessment includes the individual's history of addictive behaviors

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization obtains the individual's history of alcohol use, drug use, nicotine use, and other addictive behaviors. The history includes the following information: Age of onset; Method of acquiring substance; Duration; Patterns of use (for example, continuous, episodic, binge); Frequency, amounts, and route of the substance that is taken
findings.finding: Comprehensive substance use history is documented including all required elements for alcohol, opioids, and benzodiazepines with specific details on onset, patterns, frequency, amounts, and routes.

citations.text: Alcohol: onset age 15, current daily use 750mL-1L vodka for past 2 years, morning drinking to prevent withdrawal. Opioids: onset age 22 with prescribed Percocet, transitioned to heroin age 24, IV fentanyl age 28, current use 1-2g IV fentanyl daily. Benzodiazepines: onset age 25, initially prescribed, escalated to 4-6mg alprazolam daily through multiple prescribers and street sources.
citations.relevance: Documents age of onset, patterns, frequency, amounts, and acquisition methods for all substances

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The assessment includes the following: Consequences of substance use; Physical problems related to use; Family substance use history; Spirituality and cultural factors; Readiness to change; Current living arrangements
findings.finding: Most required elements are documented including consequences, physical problems, family history, and readiness to change. However, spirituality and cultural factors are inadequately assessed.

citations.text: Occupational: Unemployed 18 months, terminated from pharmacy technician position following diversion investigation. Unable to maintain employment due to substance use.
citations.relevance: Documents consequences of substance use

citations.text: Physical: Underweight (BMI 18.2), track marks bilateral antecubital fossae and left hand, elevated liver enzymes (AST 187, ALT 142), thrombocytopenia (platelets 98K), Hepatitis C positive.
citations.relevance: Documents physical problems related to use

citations.text: Beliefs/practices to incorporate into therapy: None identified at this time. Patient was raised Catholic but has no current practice.
citations.relevance: Shows minimal spiritual assessment

findings.remediation: Complete comprehensive cultural assessment and explore spiritual resources that could support recovery, even if patient currently reports no spiritual practices

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: Assessments of the individual served contain information about the following: Previous care, treatment, or services; Response to previous care, treatment, or services; Current risks and history of risks related to substance use; Acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential; Needs related to medications for substance use disorders
findings.finding: All required elements are comprehensively documented including detailed previous treatment history, responses to treatment, current risks, withdrawal assessment, and medication needs.

citations.text: Five prior treatment episodes: (1) 2021 — 7-day medical detox for alcohol, completed, relapsed within 48 hours. (2) 2022 — 28-day residential for opioids, AMA discharge on day 19 after conflict with staff. (3) 2023 — IOP for 6 weeks, dropped out citing transportation barriers.
citations.relevance: Documents previous treatment and responses

citations.text: Two prior overdose events in past 18 months. Has self-administered Narcan twice.
citations.relevance: Documents current risks related to substance use

citations.text: CIWA-Ar: 18. COWS: 14. BAC 0.31 in ED.
citations.relevance: Documents acute intoxication and withdrawal potential assessment

standards.standard_name: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The individual served is placed in the appropriate level of care

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization uses an evidence-based, multidimensional admission assessment that includes, at a minimum, mental health, medical, and substance-use history for placement of the individual at the appropriate level of care
findings.finding: The assessment comprehensively addresses mental health, medical, and substance use history with appropriate ASAM level 4.0 placement determination based on medical complexity and withdrawal risk.

citations.text: Patient presents with severe polysubstance use disorder requiring ASAM Level 4.0 medically managed intensive inpatient care. Concurrent alcohol and benzodiazepine dependence with seizure history creates high risk for complicated withdrawal requiring medical monitoring.
citations.relevance: Documents evidence-based level of care determination using ASAM criteria

citations.text: Co-occurring PTSD and Major Depressive Disorder with chronic passive suicidal ideation.
citations.relevance: Documents mental health assessment informing level of care

citations.text: Chronic HCV-related liver disease with elevated enzymes (AST 187, ALT 142, GGT 312). Thrombocytopenia (platelets 98K). Prior DVT right leg (2024).
citations.relevance: Documents medical complexity supporting intensive level of care

standards.standard_name: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization uses drug testing to promote safety and quality of care

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization follows its written policy on performing drug testing
findings.finding: While drug testing was performed (admission UDS documented), there is no reference to or documentation of following written policies regarding drug testing procedures.
findings.remediation: Document that drug testing was performed according to written organizational policy and reference the specific policy followed

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization documents in the individual's clinical/case record the reason for drug testing, the results, and actions based on the results
findings.finding: Drug testing results are documented but the specific reason for testing and actions taken based on results are not clearly documented.

citations.text: Admission UDS positive for fentanyl, oxycodone, benzodiazepines (alprazolam metabolites), and THC. BAC 0.31 on ED presentation.
citations.relevance: Documents drug testing results

findings.remediation: Document the reason for admission drug testing (e.g., standard admission protocol) and any clinical actions taken based on positive results

recommendations: Document that patient rights were provided and explained to patient, including receipt of written rights information
Develop process to re-inform patients of rights when capacity is restored; document when rights were re-communicated after cognitive clearing
Document assessment of patient's comprehension level and communication adaptations made; ensure information is provided at appropriate literacy level
Document communication adaptations made for patients with cognitive impairments; ensure information delivery accounts for concentration and comprehension limitations
Document patient education regarding right to refuse treatment; establish clear process for handling treatment refusals in accordance with regulations
Implement and document comprehensive informed consent process covering all required elements: proposed treatments, goals, benefits, risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusing treatment
Document that patient was informed of primary clinician and treatment team members; establish process to communicate staff roles and responsibilities to patients
Implement authentication system requiring electronic or written signatures for all clinical record entries
Establish and document written policy for timely clinical record entry and ensure compliance documentation in patient records
Complete discharge summary upon patient discharge including all required elements: reason for admission, treatment provided, discharge condition, and discharge instructions
Establish and document formal processes for information sharing with external providers, including standardized transfer forms and protocols for receiving information from referring providers
Implement and document formal patient education sessions addressing the patient's specific substance use disorders, trauma history, and medical conditions with content tailored to her abilities
Conduct and document formal learning needs assessment addressing cultural/religious beliefs, emotional barriers, motivation to learn, cognitive limitations, and communication barriers
Provide and document comprehensive patient education covering treatment plan, health practices and safety, medication management, nutritional needs, and recovery techniques
Document educational content delivery methods and ensure materials are presented in understandable format appropriate to patient's cognitive abilities and educational level
audit.audit_summary: Audit of 41 standards (104 EPs). 9 standards compliant, 32 non-compliant. EP scores: 21 satisfactory, 37 partial, 46 insufficient. Overall compliance: 20.2%.
